text.p: A last-minute rush for the public share offer of Kenya's leading tourism concern Serena Lodges & Hotels racked up sales and brokers said it was oversubscribed.
"At this stage, you could say it's comfortably oversubscribed," said Amish Gupta of sponsoring brokerage house Shah, Munge and Partners. The offer closed on Monday.
He said Shah, Munge sold 5.8 million shares -- 64 percent of the total share issue. Out of this, 72 percent of the total value was brought by individuals and 28 percent by companies.
On offer were 9,025,100 shares held by government tourism agency Kenya Tourism Development Corporation at a discounted price of 13 shillings per share.
Brokers said there was a remarkably low level of foreign interest in Serena in the primary market.
"The shares on offer were too few and it was not very clear from the prospectus exactly how many shares would be allocated to foreign investors," one broker said.
He speculated the political and foreign exchange risk associated with locking up funds for the entire flotation period could have discouraged foreign investors.
"The foreign element will definitely play a role in the success of the share in the secondary market," said another broker.
